Trace, implement and test: Print Prime Numbers Upto N

Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

Original source context
// sieve of eratosthenes

#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

using namespace std;

void sieve_of_eratosthenes(int n) {
    
    // Create a boolean array and initialize all entries as true
    
    vector<bool> primes(n + 1, true);
    primes[0] = primes[1] = false; // 0 and 1 are not prime numbers

    // Start with the first prime number, which is 2
    
    for (int p = 2; p * p <= n; ++p) {
        // If primes[p] is still true, then it is a prime number
        if (primes[p]) {
            // Mark all multiples of p as false (not prime)
            
            for (int i = p * p; i <= n; i += p) {
                primes[i] = false;
            }
        }
    }

    // Print all prime numbers
    for (int p = 2; p <= n; ++p) {
        if (primes[p]) {
            cout << p << " ";
        }
    }
}

int main() {
    int n;
    cin >> n;
    sieve_of_eratosthenes(n);
    return 0;
}
